# task-4db25302: preserve solid rectangles, remove noise

## Evidence and rule

A demonstrated and accepted test for recurring task `task-4db25302` shows a noisy grid with a dominant background color, two solid monochromatic rectangular objects, and scattered single-cell noise of various colors. The transformation removes all non-background speckles and restores/keeps each rectangle as a completely filled solid block in its object color. Preserve the original grid dimensions and background.

Demo 1: 23×18, background color 3. The valid objects were a 5×5 rectangle of color 0 at rows 0–4, columns 3–7, and a 5×6 rectangle of color 1 at rows 1–5, columns 12–17. Scattered non-background marks outside the rectangles and occasional marks inside them were noise; output was exactly background 3 except for these full rectangles.

Accepted test: 11×26, background 6. Valid objects were color 8 rectangle rows 3–4, columns 15–21 (2×7) and color 5 rectangle rows 5–10, columns 6–11 (6×6). Scattered 4s were noise, including points within the object footprints; the accepted output removed all noise and retained/fill-completed those rectangles.

## Solving procedure

1. Identify the dominant background color.
2. Find the two coherent, dense, axis-aligned monochrome rectangular regions; distinguish them from sparse isolated marks (noise), even if a noise cell interrupts the rectangle.
3. Use each rectangle's bounding box and its object color to fill the full solid rectangle.
4. Set every other cell to background, including all scattered colors and any noise outside the rectangles.
5. Preserve exact input dimensions and validate every row width before submitting.

## Caution

Only one demo and one accepted test establish this branch. Do not assume a fixed palette, rectangle size, or location. Infer these anew from each fresh input; if the objects are ambiguous, request a demo rather than treating arbitrary sparse marks as part of a rectangle."
}
